## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to craft per-host reporting with minimal tools, handling spaces in paths and unreadable dirs, while operating on large file sets. It checks command composition, correct use of find predicates (-size, -mtime), and safe shell looping.

## Key Concepts
- find -type f -size +1M -mtime -7
- shell loop over host dirs
- 2>/dev/null to skip unreadable dirs
- per-host aggregation and formatted output

## Code Example
```bash
for d in /data/vhosts/*; do
  [ -d "$d" ] || continue
  host=$(basename "$d")
  echo -n "$host "
  find "$d" -type f -size +1M -mtime -7 2>/dev/null | wc -l
done
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you handle extremely large directories or network-mounted paths?
- How would you extend this to output JSON or CSV for automation?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to handle mixed log formats, gzipped archives, and nested paths, while producing precise per-hour, per-service aggregates in a single pass.

## Key Concepts
- Robust parsing for text and JSON lines without external libs
- Decompressing .gz on the fly (zcat) and skipping unreadable files
- Deriving service from path or JSON field
- Time bucketing by hour and rolling window (12h)
- Streaming aggregation with POSIX AWK

## Code Example
```bash
find /logs -type f \( -name '*.log' -o -name '*.log.gz' \) -print0 | \
  xargs -0 -I{} sh -lc 'f="{}"; case "${f##*.}" in gz) zcat "$f" 2>/dev/null || true ;; *) cat "$f" 2>/dev/null || true ;; esac' | \
  awk 'BEGIN{FS=""; OFS=","}
       /\[|{"ts":/ {/* parse via simple regex; normalize to ts,lvl,service */}
       }' 2>/dev/null | \
  sort -u | \
  awk 'BEGIN{FS=",";OFS=","} {hour=substr($1,1,13)"0"; service=$2; count[$hour","$service]+=($3=="ERROR"||$3=="CRITICAL")} END{for(k in count) print k","count[k]}' | \
  sort
```

## Why This Is Asked

- Per-object aggregation with awk

```bash
find /logs/app -type f -mtime -7 -print0 2>/dev/null | \
  while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do \
    svc=$(basename "$(dirname "$f")"); \
    s=$(stat -c%s "$f" 2>/dev/null); \
    [ -n "$s" ] && echo "$svc:$s"; \
  done | awk -F':' '{sum[$1]+=$2} END{for (k in sum) print k":"sum[k]}' | \
```
